_about: How the Takemikazuchi's arms are put on Ronin's first-person arm files (what the pilot sees from the cockpit):
The arms are the approved body fit's own arm triangles (level 0), not a second fit.
Hands: Ronin's first-person rig has its wrist and finger joints exactly where the body rig has them
(within 0.02 unit), so every hand and finger vertex keeps its place on its bone: the cockpit hand is the
Upper arm and forearm: the first-person rig's elbow sits 8.6 units nearer the wrist and its shoulder joint
5.7 units further out than on the body (Ronin's own first-person arms are built that way).  Each section is
therefore laid between the first-person joints the same way the body fit lays it between the body's joints:
length along the bone follows the joints, thickness is untouched.
Which of Ronin's finger joints turns each finger piece.  The Takemikazuchi's hand is smaller than Ronin's,
so the knuckle of a finger piece (its inner end) is not at the Ronin joint the body fit hangs it on, and a
curled finger comes apart.  Each piece is turned by the joint of the same finger that sits at its inner end
(within this many units); a piece with no joint there stays rigid with the piece it grows from.
Nothing is moved or resized; the hand at rest is the body's hand.  rule: 'as_on_the_body' keeps the body

checks._about: the build stops if a hand vertex would move by more than this many units against the body fit
